purpose: Assess whether JICA's Lower Cagayan River Annex V can serve as an independently gathered fish-species source, while separating its aggregate ecological summary from fishery catch statistics and preserving reuse limits.

source.title: The feasibility study of the flood control project for the lower Cagayan River in the Republic of the Philippines: Final Report, Volume III-1 Supporting Report, Annex V Environment
source.provider: Japan International Cooperation Agency; Nippon Koei Co., Ltd.; NIKKEN Consultants, Inc.
source.citation: Japan International Cooperation Agency, Nippon Koei Co., Ltd., & NIKKEN Consultants, Inc. (2002, February). The feasibility study of the flood control project for the lower Cagayan River in the Republic of the Philippines: Final Report, Volume III-1 Supporting Report, Annex V Environment, sections 1.4 and 2.1.
source.license: The JICA catalog states Copyright © JICA. All rights reserved. No item-specific open reuse terms were found.

reviewedEvidence.aquaticEcology: Section 1.4.2 reports 141 total aquatic taxa for the Cagayan River system: 44 phytoplankton, 18 zooplankton, 15 benthos, 47 fishes, seven macro-crustaceans, and ten molluscs. It says the total would likely be higher after more thorough sampling. This is an aggregate report statement, not a complete checklist or a modern estimate.
reviewedEvidence.fisheriesCatch: Section 2.1.2 says a Cagayan State University study monitored catch in 1998 at Aparri, Camalaniugan, Lal-lo, and Gattaran. Table 2.1.3 presents monthly catch composition in kilograms, but its source note cites Assessment and Biology of Fisheries Researches in Cagayan River and Abulog River (1990). The reviewed report does not resolve whether the displayed table is the 1998 monitoring result, a 1990 source table, or a re-use of the earlier work.
reviewedEvidence.fieldMetadata: The aquatic ecology subsection points to a seven-site map and a sampling-sites table. The reviewed report text does not supply fish collection dates, methods, vouchers, or accession IDs. The map depicts site symbols but no exact coordinates; they were not digitized.
reviewedEvidence.overallSchedule: The main report describes JICA study-team visits from March 2000 through December 2001 and a final report in February 2002. This broad project schedule is not evidence of specific fish sampling dates.

qualityAndReuseLimits: The 47-fish figure is an aggregate report statement and cannot be expanded into 47 source-verified species names from this review.
Figure 1.4.1's distribution legend contains common and vernacular names and is introduced in the secondary-data subsection; it is not a voucher-linked species-by-site occurrence table.
Figure 1.4.2 provides seven named site labels but not coordinate-precision metadata. No points or river geometries were generated from it.
No sampling method, event date, fish voucher, catalog number, or genetic accession was established for the 47-fish total.
The catch table has unresolved 1998-versus-1990 provenance and common-name-only categories. It is not promoted to species-occurrence evidence or a current catch baseline.
The report contains historical conservation and regulation statements. They are not current legal, fishing-season, safety, or conservation advice.
JICA's report catalog states all rights reserved. No item-specific open license was identified. No table, map, figure, species list, or data rows are reproduced; app projection is not approved.

relationshipToOtherSources.jica2023BfarCrosscheck: This 2002 feasibility annex is a separate historical report. Do not confuse its aggregate aquatic survey summary or 1990/1998 catch discussion with the 2023 JICA planning report that repeats BFAR Region II's 2006 list.
relationshipToOtherSources.ludongTaxonomy: The report uses the historical label Cestraeus plicatilis and dated conservation statements. Later reviewed NFRDI evidence identifies sampled Northern Luzon ludong as Cestraeus goldiei; the old report is not independently re-identifying specimens or resolving the historical name concept.
relationshipToOtherSources.underlyingCatchStudy: The 1990 Assessment and Biology of Fisheries Researches in Cagayan River and Abulog River cited by the table was not located as an openly accessible full-text source during this review.

nextAction: Continue Region II source discovery using openly accessible university and journal repositories. Search for the underlying 1990 Cagayan-Abulog fisheries study and the full 2023 UPV ICFAS poster or 2024 Cagayan Basin presentation, then prioritize recent freshwater, reservoir, wetland, estuary, and brackish fish work with named sites, vouchers/accessions, and explicit reuse terms.
